candidates.explanation: I couldn't open the files, so this is inferred from how the boilerplate is usually written. When the domain user has no photo (photo is undefined, as in a first-name-only update), toPersistence most likely sets photo to null instead of leaving it undefined. TypeORM then saves the null and clears the avatar relation. Only an explicit null should clear the photo. An undefined photo should leave the property unset so the update keeps the existing value.

The photo handling here may turn an omitted photo into null. The photo variable should stay undefined when the payload has no photo, be null only when the payload sends null, and be a file object when an id is given. If the code falls through to null, or always passes photo to the repository, a partial update wipes the avatar.

The update builds the entity by spreading the mapped payload over the existing one. If it overwrites the existing photo with an undefined or null value from the partial payload, the avatar is lost. It should keep the existing photo unless the payload explicitly sets one.

fix.description: In toPersistence, set persistenceEntity.photo to a FileEntity only when domainEntity.photo is truthy. Set it to null only when domainEntity.photo === null. Leave it undefined otherwise so partial updates keep the existing avatar. In UsersService.update, keep the local photo variable undefined unless the payload has a photo id or an explicit null.
